d: Gil Favor single handedly seeks revenge when members of a masked organization horsewhip him and lynch one of his drovers.
The drive runs into trouble when an U.S. Army dam project halts the herd and trail boss Gil Favor is accused of murder.
A bank president takes trail boss Gil Favors place and Favor becomes head of the bank.
A professional hangman learns that the man he has been sent to execute is the town's most popular and powerful citizen.
A condemned man makes a drastic decision when he realized attempts to thwart his hanging would cause a bloody conflict.
Gil Favor is shot in the back when he refuses to accept a beautiful woman's story that she is innocent of a murder charge.
The drovers hire a man they later learn is a fugitive from a U.S. Army general court martial.
A strange Indian tribe captures Hey Soos and forces him to drink a non-fatal poison.
Rowdy Yates leaves the Favor cattle drive, gets a herd of his own and takes on his former boss in a race to a railhead.
Trail boss Gil Favor receives a marriage proposal and a threat of death, both from the same family.
A bankrupt cattle baron plans to recoup his ranch lands with money stolen from a bank.
Gil Favors reputation as trail boss is jeopardized when he starts a drive with a herd of cattle and ends it with nine head.

st: Incident of a Man Called Mushy
d: Slow-witted Mushy is duped by four gypsies who convince him they are the rightful owners of the wagons and horses he is guarding.
Gil Favor unwittingly involves his drovers in a scheme which finds them working fora railroad instead of herding cattle.
Railroad boss Jonathan Damon convinces the drovers that cattle droving is passed railroading is the thing of the future.
Rowdy Yates is accused of shooting a man in the back and faces death when he tries to carry out the dying man's last request.
An Army corporal finds himself in charge of a squad of men of which he is the weakest member.
